title: Historic Vellulla Tank Reveals 1613 Telugu Inscription and Ancient Sculpture

One of the most important discoveries is a Telugu inscription beside [...]HYDERABAD: A historic tank on the outskirts of Vellulla village in Metpalli mandal is preserving archaeological remains that date from the 12th to the 17th centuries. According to historian and heritage researcher Karipe Raj Kumar, the site offers valuable insights into the region's history. One of the most important discoveries is a Telugu inscription beside the sluice on the tank bund. The inscription says Minnayya, a member of the Munnuru community, built the sluice as an offering to Lord Narasimha. He completed the work under the patronage of Dalapati Rayudu, described as the "Moon of the Velama community." The inscription records that the sluice was built on Vaishakha Shuddha Panchami, a Thursday, in the Pramadi year of the Shalivahana Era 1535. The date corresponds to April 15, 1613 CE. It also identifies Dalapati Rayudu as the Mutalik (administrator) of Padmanayaka ruler Vengala Jagadeva. A weathered 12th-century sculpture of Kala Bhairava stands above the sluice. The deity appears in the tribhanga posture. The sculpture shows a sword and a blood bowl in the front hands, while the rear hands hold a damaru (drum) and a trident. It also features flaming locks of hair and a girdle of skulls around the waist. Raj Kumar also pointed to a Kakatiya-period sculpture of Ellamma on the outskirts of Vellulla village. He said the sculpture remains exposed to the weather and risks further damage. He urged the authorities to collect and preserve the sculptures, inscriptions, and hero stones at a common heritage site. He said this would help protect the region's archaeological legacy for future generations. ]]>

title: “One in a Million” Find: Soft Tissue Discovered in 450-Million-Year-Old Fossil
